root_cause.text: The net/core forwarding-path resolver used WARN_ON_ONCE on the user-influenced net_device_path_stack index in dev_fwd_path(), so an excessively long forwarding path could trigger a kernel warning by exceeding NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX instead of being handled as a normal bounds check failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch in net/core/dev.c changes `if (WARN_ON_ONCE(k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX))` to `if (k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX)`, and the commit message states that “userspace manages to build a sufficiently long forward path” and that recent IPIP tunnel support increases the chance of reaching this warning.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet directly contains the relevant logic in `dev_fwd_path()`. It increments the user-influenced path index with `int k = stack->num_paths++;` and then checks bounds using `if (WARN_ON_ONCE(k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX)) return NULL;`. This matches the root cause: exceeding `NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX` triggers a kernel warning instead of being handled as a normal bounds check failure. The caller `dev_fill_forward_path()` repeatedly invokes `dev_fwd_path(stack)` inside a loop while walking forwarding devices, so an excessively long forwarding path can drive `stack->num_paths` beyond the limit and hit the warning. There is no non-warning bounds check here, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet applied.
